title: Kitchener indoor recreation complex design and budget
subtitle: Glen Road permit parking stays, three environmental assessments advance, Tier 2 community grants and Creative Hub rates recommended.
overview: The committee recommended an upgraded Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex, with a total budget of $143,820,000 and a goal of being the City's first net-zero carbon facility {{vote:m11}}. The design adds a larger turf field and leisure pool, a walking track, viewing galleries and a cricket batting cage. Staff said the project would be paid for by grants and development charges, not property taxes.

Three environmental assessments moved ahead: the Blair Creek Drive extension {{vote:m8}}, Hidden Valley flood risk reduction {{vote:m9}} and the Schneider and Shoemaker creeks naturalization {{vote:m10}}. Each now goes to a 30-day public review.

On Glen Road, the committee did not recommend removing permit-only parking {{vote:m6}}, so the current rules stay for now. It also recommended Tier 2 community grants totalling $209,415 {{vote:m1}}, a Creative Hub rent schedule {{vote:m4}} and no-parking rules on Parkvale Drive {{vote:m3}}. These are recommendations, and Council will make the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended the improved design, a net-zero carbon target, a $143,820,000 budget with $47,915,000 in added debenture financing repaid from development charges, and a supplementary agreement with the project team {{vote:m11}}.
The committee received the Schedule B environmental assessment report, which prefers Alternative 2, and recommended filing it for the 30-day review period.
The committee received the environmental assessment report preferring Alternative 4, a larger culvert at Hidden Valley Road, and recommended filing it for the 30-day review.
The committee recommended approving the environmental study report, posting it for 30-day review, and proceeding to detailed design of Stage 1 afterward.
A motion to remove permit-only parking on Glen Road from South Drive to Pleasant Avenue was lost {{vote:m6}}, leaving the existing permit rules in place.
The committee recommended approving Tier 2 community grants totalling $209,415.
The committee recommended endorsing the tenant rate schedule and skills trade protocols, and authorizing staff to sign licence agreements of two years or less with tenants.
The committee recommended prohibiting on-street parking on both sides of Parkvale Drive from Huron Road to a point 65 metres west.

debate: On Glen Road, two delegates asked for more consultation. They said the resident-led petition missed some households and did not explain the downsides. They also warned that free parking near the hospital and two parks could crowd out residents.

Staff said the petition showed majority support: 19 of 35 addresses in favour. They said supporters were phoned to confirm, every address got a letter, and a nearby street had its permits removed in 2014 without complaints. They said the road is wide enough for emergency access and the hospital was not consulted.

Some members wanted to defer the Glen Road item to consult the hospital and run a City-led survey. Others said the hospital was not central. Staff said a survey would likely not draw more responses and could not be done before June or July. Staff also cautioned that talking to the hospital could widen the review to other streets.

On the recreation complex, staff and members said the Integrated Project Delivery model shares risk, with profit at stake if costs rise. They stressed that funding comes from grants and development charges, not property taxes. Staff said using these charges would limit funding for other growth-related recreation facilities for years.

Members asked why the complex has no ice rinks and whether the money could go to housing. Staff said an arena was not among the 2019 priorities and an arena strategy is under way. They said the grants and development charges are restricted to recreation facilities.
